episodes.181196: A weak disturbance generated a few afternoon thunderstorms, one of which reached severe levels.
episodes.181273: On the late evening of July 25, a supercell developed in the eastern Dakotas and moved into west central Minnesota. This supercell grew upscale into a small bow echo as it moved east/southeast into central and eventually eastern Minnesota during the overnight hours of the 25th into the 26th. The storm produced a damage swath about 1 to 2 counties wide, with some enhanced damage from near Stevens County down through the Stearns/Kandiyohi county line. There was also a brief EF0 tornado near New London.
episodes.181361: After high pressure dominated eastern Utah for a couple of days, moisture gradually increased ahead of an approaching system. This led to the development of isolated to scattered high-based thunderstorms. Given the dry air at the lower levels, gusty outflow winds were the primary threat from storms. The stronger storms produced gusty winds in excess of 58 mph across Uintah County.
episodes.181407: A line of showers and thunderstorms with strong outflow winds moved across south-central and southeast Wyoming during the afternoon on the 26th.
episodes.181612: A complex of thunderstorms crossing Lake Erie pushed across western New York during the evening hours. The storms produced sporadic wind damage over western New York before weakening as they tracked farther east.
episodes.181613: A complex of thunderstorms crossing Lake Erie pushed across western New York during the evening hours. The storms produced sporadic wind damage over western New York before weakening as they tracked farther east.
episodes.181651: Multiple clusters of storms tracked over the southern half of Lake Michigan during the morning and early afternoon hours. Access ramps, boat slips and piers were damaged at Reefpoint Marina when strong thunderstorm winds moved through the Marina. 40-60 boats broke free but were retrieved.
episodes.181718: Lightning struck a tree, causing the wood to split and fall onto a person near Lake Waccamaw.
episodes.181753: Thunderstorms developed near a warm front surging north during the evening hours on Tuesday (7/25) across northeast Wisconsin.  The strongest storm produced wind damage.
episodes.181894: Remnant outflow from convection the day before over the Midwest combined with a lee pressure trough resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Several produced localized wind damage and some hail.
episodes.181895: Remnant outflow from convection the day before over the Midwest combined with a lee pressure trough resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Several produced localized wind damage and some hail.
episodes.181943: Remnant outflow from convection the day before over the Midwest combined with a lee pressure trough resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Several produced localized gale- to storm-force winds over area waterways.
episodes.182059: A warm front draped across central Illinois aided the development of clusters of thunderstorms during the evening, primarily to the east of I-55. These thunderstorms produced scattered large hail, the largest of which was 2.5 inches in diameter in Douglas County, as well as isolated damaging winds.
episodes.182071: A microburst over Page Field in Fort Myers produced a strong wind gust.
episodes.182294: Numerous strong nocturnal thunderstorms formed over the western Midwest during the night of the 25th-26th.  Freezing levels around 14,000 feet and nearly 1800 J/kg of MUCAPE promoted marginally severe hail in Morgan County, while mid-level dry air and 0-3 km wind shear over 30 kts supported isolated damaging winds across Vermillion and Putnam Counties.
episodes.182330: A warm front and upper level disturbance led to lines and clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms across southern WI. Mostly tree damage was observed.
episodes.182485: Two EF-0 tornadoes struck portions of Jackson county on July 26th resulting in some damage mostly to trees and some crops.  Severe storms also produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.182539: Thunderstorms developed in an environment of strong instability ahead of an advancing cold front. One storm split, and the left moving cell from this split produced very strong winds estimated at 90 mph resulting in damage through south central North Dakota. A farm in far southeastern Morton County near Breien sustained heavy damage, especially to the barn. The storm then continued to the northeast and passed through Steele, where multiple trees were blown over and many large tree limbs were broken.
episodes.182921: Two areas of thunderstorms brought severe weather to central and northeast South Dakota on the evening of July 25th. A warm front across northeastern South Dakota provided the focus for storms that generated at least one observed wind gust of 63 mph. A secondary area of thunderstorms developed over central South Dakota near a surface low-pressure system. The thunderstorms that developed over Hand County resulted in quarter-size hail, winds in excess of 60 mph, and a brief tornado that produced EF0 damage.
episodes.182979: A cluster of storms that produced multiple wind gusts over 60 mph moved through northwest Kansas in the late evening and overnight hours of the 25th.
episodes.183137: A shortwave combined with a weak low level jet produced isolated severe storms along the Cook County shoreline. These storms produced hail the size of quarters along with tree damage along the Cascade River.
episodes.183138: A shortwave combined with a weak low level jet produced isolated severe storms along the Cook County shoreline. These storms produced hail the size of quarters along with tree damage along the Cascade River.
episodes.183160: Storms in the late hours of July 25th and into the early morning hours of July 26th caused dangerous wind gusts and hail in Northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.183162: Storms in the late hours of July 25th caused high wind gusts in southeastern North Dakota. These storms continued to produce high winds and even hail as they moved into Minnesota.
episodes.183172: Strong thunderstorms produced winds in excess of 40 mph along the tip of the Keweenaw Peninsula on the morning of the 26th.
episodes.183274: A shortwave brushed across northern Iowa through the early morning hours of July 26th. Despite warm mid levels, storms were fueled by the low level jet and moved along a moderate instability gradient of 1500 J/kg of CAPE.  While most storms remained sub-severe, one storm across Pocahontas county strengthened to produce quarter sized hail.
episodes.183275: A line of thunderstorms developed ahead of a frontal boundary and moved across Lake Michigan during the morning hours of July 26, 2023. These thunderstorms would eventually track across the state into a very warm and unstable environment. The southern end of the line of storms is where the strongest winds associated with the line would develop and moved across the lower portions of southeast Michigan during the afternoon between 2 PM and 5 PM. A swath of widespread 60-70 mph wind gusts with locally higher gusts resulted in numerous downed trees, downed powerlines, and around 165,000 power outages in southeast Michigan. The Ann Arbor and the Detroit/Grosse Pointe areas were hit the hardest.
episodes.183278: An isolated thunderstorm brought mostly nickel-sized hail, with a few quarters mixed in as well.
episodes.183279: An area of low pressure and associated cold front brought thunderstorms to central and north central South Dakota during the evening hours on July 26th. Golf ball to tennis ball size hail broke multiple windows and caused damage to property seven miles south-southeast of Chantier Creek Recreation area.
episodes.183466: Scattered supercells across southwest Nebraska resulted in large hail and strong winds during the late afternoon and early evening hours of July 26.
episodes.183508: A broken line of isolated strong to marginally severe storms moved through the area on the morning of July 26. Storms produced severe wind gusts in eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois, with some reports of small hail.
episodes.183509: A broken line of isolated strong to marginally severe storms moved through the area on the morning of July 26. Storms produced severe wind gusts in eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois, with some reports of small hail.
episodes.183529: Sufficient moisture continued to flow through the region in late July, leading to daytime convection most days. This convection was occasionally strong to severe, yielding localized strong wind gusts in addition to flash flooding.
episodes.183785: A severe thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size south of Elbert.
episodes.183805: Multiple rounds of convection occurred. The first round of storms intensified arriving into northern Indiana and southern Michigan, resulting in wind damage along and north of US 6. Another round of damaging winds and heavy rainfall occurred across southern Lower Michigan later in the day. Storms continued to back build into the evening. Locally heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches occurred across southern Lower Michigan.
episodes.183807: Multiple rounds of convection occurred. The first round of storms intensified arriving into northern Indiana and southern Michigan, resulting in wind damage along and north of US 6. Another round of damaging winds and heavy rainfall occurred across southern Lower Michigan later in the day. Storms continued to back build into the evening. Locally heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches occurred across southern Lower Michigan.
episodes.183810: Thundestorms moving through Lake St. Clair and Detroit River produced wind gusts in excess of 50 knots.
episodes.183849: Multiple rounds of convection occurred. The first round of storms intensified arriving into northern Indiana and southern Michigan, resulting in wind damage along and north of US 6. Another round of damaging winds and heavy rainfall occurred across southern Lower Michigan later in the day. Storms continued to back build into the evening. episodes.183874: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west across Pima, Pinal and Santa Cruz counties during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorm winds damaged homes on the Tohono O'odham Nation.
episodes.183875: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west from Cochise and Santa Cruz across Pima and Pinal counties during the afternoon and evening.  Thunderstorm winds produced a dust storm in Pinal County.
episodes.183892: An isolated storm developed in the axis of greatest instability consisting of 1500+ J/kg MLCAPE and 1000 J/kg DCAPE.  For a couple hours, a balance of shear and instability supported a long track of damaging winds and spotty large hail from near Miller southeast to near Beresford. Measured winds from 60 to 80 mph were common.
episodes.183895: An elevated storm developed across east central South Dakota and moved into southwest Minnesota before weakening. The storm briefly produced marginally large hail near Magnolia.
episodes.183896: An isolated storm developed in the axis of greatest elevated instability around 1000 J/kg CAPE and dropped occasional large hail moving southeast across northwest Iowa.
episodes.183921: During the late afternoon hours, thunderstorms developed along a boundary near the Kansas-Nebraska border. One particular storm strengthened over the Dundy-Hitchcock county line, moving over the town of Stratton as it produced pea to penny hail.
episodes.183928: A linear cluster of storms developed off the Front Range moving east across Northwest Kansas during the evening hours. The storms produced thunderstorm wind gusts up to 100 mph as they moved through, with the strongest gusts reported in the town of McDonald in Rawlins County. Damage occurred primarily to trees in portions of Cheyenne and Rawlins counties with additional damage to powerlines, campers, and structures. The thunderstorm wind gusts and the outflow of the storm also created dust storm conditions with visibilities of one-quarter mile or less observed in Cheyenne, Sherman, and Rawlins counties. Blowing dust with visibility reductions of three to five miles were also observed near the cities of Colby and Oakley.
episodes.183960: Numerous gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with a cluster of thunderstorms that moved southwest off the south Florida mainland.  A deep Saharan Air Layer was exiting the Florida Keys coastal waters to the west.
episodes.183961: Deep tropical moisture surging northward in confluent lower tropospheric flow enhanced by the presence of a tropical upper tropospheric tutt (TUTT) cell over western Cuba supported scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across the eastern Straits of Florida through Florida Bay.
episodes.183992: An isolated supercell developed along a dry line and produced a tornado.
episodes.184004: A cold front moved across central Wyoming on July 26th and brought showers and thunderstorms that brought strong to damaging winds for portions of Fremont and Natrona Counties. The most intense storm occurred in Fremont County. There were numerous wind gusts over 58 mph and some gusts as high as 74 mph. Numerous limbs and trees were downed on the west side of Riverton, including at the Riverton Country Club. Wind gusts as high as 68 mph occurred in Natrona County as well as the line of thunderstorms moved eastward.
episodes.184201: A passing cold front brought strong storms to northern Illinois during the morning of July 26th. While these storms mostly remained sub-severe, they produced several instances of tree and power line damage. One man was also injured when he was reportedly struck by lightning.
episodes.184254: Thunderstorms moved into Traverse County during the late evening hours. The storms produced tree damage in Wheaton and a 59 mph wind gust 6 miles west-southwest of Wheaton.
episodes.184379: A line of strong to severe storms moved through southeast Minnesota during the early morning hours of July 26th. While the line of storms spanned Dodge County to Winona County, a narrow swath of damaging winds impacted parts of Olmsted County. Reports included 60 mph winds recorded at the Rochester International Airport as well as multiple fallen trees near Rochester and Byron.
episodes.184384: Strong to severe storms progressed east through the Upper Mississippi River Valley during the overnight hours of July 25th, reaching western Wisconsin in the early morning hours of July 26th. Multiple reports of damaging winds accompanied the bowing line of storms as it progressed through the Upper Mississippi River Valley into western Wisconsin with varying intensity. Reports included a torn off barn roof near Platteville (Grant County) and snapped trees near Tomah (Monroe County) and Platteville (Grant County).
episodes.184398: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.184399: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.184661: During the evening a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 MPH was measured near Heartstrong.  Earlier in the evening the thunderstorm activity had started atleast two fires further south in Cheyenne County.  No damage was reported with these fires.
episodes.185769: A surface low moved northeastward from central Lower MI to Georgian Bay during the early afternoon through late evening of the 26th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from southeastern Lower MI, western and central Lake Erie, and far-eastern OH to the Upper Saint Lawrence River Valley and far-northern NY. Within the warm sector, multiple lines and clusters of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward across northern OH, in vicinity of a surface trough axis, and generated scattered straight-line convective wind damage, a measured severe convective wind gust, and an instance of severe hail. These storms encountered moderate to strong effective bulk shear and primarily moderate to strong MUCAPE.
episodes.185844: A surface low moved northeastward from central Lower MI to Georgian Bay during the early afternoon through late evening of the 26th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from southeastern Lower MI, western and central Lake Erie, and far-eastern OH to the Upper Saint Lawrence River Valley and far-northern NY. Within the warm sector, a line of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward across northwest PA, in vicinity of a surface trough axis. These storms generated isolated straight-line convective wind damage. Three people were injured by a downed tree in Presque Isle State Park. The storms encountered moderate to strong effective bulk shear and primarily moderate to strong MUCAPE.
episodes.185845: A surface low moved northeastward from central Lower MI to Georgian Bay during the early afternoon through late evening of the 26th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from southeastern Lower MI, western and central Lake Erie, and far-eastern OH to the Upper Saint Lawrence River Valley and far-northern NY. Within the warm sector, multiple lines and clusters of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward across Lake Erie, in vicinity of a surface trough axis. These storms generated scattered gale-force and storm-force convective wind gusts along the OH and PA shore of Lake Erie as they encountered moderate to strong effective bulk shear and primarily moderate to strong MUCAPE.
episodes.186196: A cluster of thunderstorms brought heavy rain and strong winds over southern Lake Michigan during the morning of the 26th.

A brief tornado formed along a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) and moved into New London. It took part of the roof off of three homes and a large shed. Other homes sustained shingle, soffit, and siding damage. At least 200 trees were broken or uprooted. Some of the adjacent damage appeared to be associated with inflow winds. The tornado was associated with a surge in the QLCS which then caused damaging downburst winds that started several miles west of New London and continued into Meeker County (see separate entries).

A brief EF-0 tornado occurred southeast of Stockbridge.  It touched down near Orchard Creek east of Fitchburg road and south of Baseline road.  Several dozen large trees were impacted with several uprooted trees along the path. Several homes on Musbach road had minor roof damage or damage from tree debris.  The tornado lifted near Dewey road.

It moved east northeast and lifted just northeast of Leeke road and north of Bowdish road.  Intermitted damage was foudn along the path primarily to trees and crops. One business along the path sustained some minor structural damage that included roof damage and siding damage to an outbuilding.
